# AGENTS.md: FundAdmin AI plugin

Instructions for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others) working with this repository. Humans: see [README.md](README.md).

## What this repository is

The published `fundadmin` plugin: 62 fund administration skills, one menu skill (`fund`) and 5 LPA-review subagents, packaged for Claude Code, Claude Cowork and Codex. Version 1.0.6, MIT. It is **generated** from `https://github.com/davendra/fundadmin-ai` and republished as a single commit per release.

## If a user asks you to install it

| Host | Do this |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude plugin marketplace add davendra/fundadmin-ai-skills` then `claude plugin install fundadmin@fundadmin-ai-skills`; tell the user to restart the session |
| Codex | `codex plugin marketplace add davendra/fundadmin-ai-skills` then `codex plugin add fundadmin@fundadmin-ai-skills` |
| Claude Cowork | Tell the user: Customize → Plugins → Add marketplace → `davendra/fundadmin-ai-skills` → install FundAdmin AI (it is a UI step; you cannot do it for them) |

Verify in Claude Code with `claude plugin details fundadmin@fundadmin-ai-skills`: expect 63 skills and 5 agents.

## If you are using the skills

1. **Pick the skill** from [`catalog.json`](catalog.json) (`skills[].description` says when each one applies) or from the table below. When unsure, run the menu skill `fund`.
2. **Invoke it**
   - Claude Code / Cowork: the Skill tool with `fundadmin:<skill-name>`, or the user types `/fundadmin:fund <command> <args>`.
   - Codex: `$<skill-name>`.
   - No skill system: read `plugins/fundadmin/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` and follow it.
3. **Inputs** are file paths (PDF, markdown, CSV, email), pasted text, or earlier outputs under `reviews/`.
4. **Outputs** are markdown files, mostly under `reviews/<fund-slug>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<subfolder>/` in the working directory, in the fixed filename family named in each skill's description (`catalog.json` → `writes`). Read the skill for its exact path.
5. **`review-lpa`** launches `fundadmin:fund-terms`, `fund-risks`, `fund-compliance` and `fund-obligations` in parallel, waits, then runs `fund-recommendations` on their results. Do not background these agents or write the report before all five return. Expect 15 to 40 minutes.
6. **`report-pdf`** needs Python 3 with `reportlab`. Without it, hand over the markdown and the command.
7. **Optional integrations** (`vault_*` MCP tools, Gmail connector) are used only when present. Skip them silently otherwise, except `monitor-email`, which must stop and say it needs Gmail.

## Rules every output follows

- Include the disclaimer: document analysis and drafting support, **not financial, legal or tax advice**.
- Describe documents; never tell anyone whether to commit or invest.
- Use the placeholders `[fund]`, `[investor]`, `[type]`, `[date]`.
- Use only the filename families the skills name; never invent new ones.
- Never attribute figures to a licensed benchmark dataset the project does not hold; the benchmark ranges in the skills are illustrative sample data.
- Files under `samples/` are synthetic. Treat them as real documents when reviewing, but never copy the synthetic banner into a report as if it were a term.

## If you are changing this repository

Don't edit files here by hand; the next release overwrites them. Make the change in `https://github.com/davendra/fundadmin-ai` (`skills/`, `fund/`, `agents/`, `tools/plugin_meta.json`, `tools/plugin/`), then run `python3 tools/build_plugin.py`. To check a checkout of this repo:

```bash
claude plugin validate --strict plugins/fundadmin
claude plugin validate --strict .
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## Agents

| Agent | Dimension | LPA Safety Score weight |
|---|---|---|
| `fundadmin:fund-terms` | Terms & Provisions | 20% |
| `fundadmin:fund-risks` | Risk Assessment | 25% |
| `fundadmin:fund-compliance` | Regulatory Compliance | 20% |
| `fundadmin:fund-obligations` | Obligations & Timeline | 15% |
| `fundadmin:fund-recommendations` | Recommendations | 20% |
